product_family: Superalloy bar, billet and remelt stock
method: 20.0 kt cobalt in superalloys (Cobalt Institute) divided by virgin cobalt content 4/8/15 percent, times 75/85/95 percent leaving as bar, billet or remelt stock. Melt tonnes, gross weight.
cross_checks: China reported output 64.5 kt in 2025 (demand about 66 kt, CO_BAOWU_CHINA_SUPERALLOY_2025, 2021 broker view) is 33 percent of the P50. ATI Monroe fifth VIM furnace adds about 9 kt a year from 2027 (ARGUS_SUPERALLOY) = 5 percent of the P50. A listed producer's high performance alloy melt of 83 kt (includes corrosion resistant grades) = 43 percent of the P50, so the range is plausible only at its upper half: the cobalt method probably understates revert rich melt.
label: team estimate, not summable (families overlap and use different stages)

product_family: Nickel alloy bar, rod and wire (long products)
method: HS 750512 plus 750522 (alloy only) exports of eight reporters 2024 = 80.3 kt (traded floor; the HS 7505 total incl. pure nickel is 82.6 kt, so alloy is 97 percent) times 1.0/1.5/2.5. EU27 PRODCOM apparent consumption 5.4 kt is a lower bound (production cell confidential) and is not used.
cross_checks: Germany alone exported 18.1 kt, the United States 31.0 kt and Italy 11.1 kt of HS 7505 in 2024 (Comtrade). INSG: stainless is just under 70 percent of 3,577 kt primary nickel use, so non stainless primary use is at most about 1,070 kt of nickel, a ceiling not a base.
label: team estimate, not summable (families overlap and use different stages)
